answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not quite yet. Jumping from 12 mi to 40 mi in one week is a bigger leap than I would take two weeks after a marathon, and starting intervals on top of that is where post-race injuries show up. A good rule of thumb is roughly one easy day per mile raced before full-intensity work, which puts you around mid-November for sharp speed.

Here is what I would do instead: this week around 20 to 24 mi with four easy runs and a few short strides, next week step toward 30 mi and add one light session (hill strides or a fartlek), then the week after you can be back near 40 mi with a proper 10K-style workout.

Before I write that next block, tell me what you actually want to race. Is it the Thanksgiving 10K your friend mentioned (that would be about four weeks out), something else, or just a return to steady training for now?

new.analysis:
## What last week showed
You followed the recovery plan exactly: three easy runs for 12 mi, all low effort, all pain-free. Easy heart rate came down from 139 to 133 bpm and Sunday felt an 8 out of 10, which is what a recovering body looks like.

## Why I am holding you back
Feeling ready and being ready are different things two weeks after a marathon. The quads that gave out at mile 20 are a signal that connective tissue took a real hit, and it rebuilds slower than the aerobic system you can already feel bouncing back. One more conservative week protects the base you just built.

## How next week fits
I am adding a fourth run and a short set of strides on Wednesday to wake the legs up without loading them. Sunday grows to 7 mi, still fully easy, as a gentle re-entry to a longer effort. If everything stays pain-free and heart rate stays where it is now, we open the throttle the week after.

## What I need from you
Pick a direction: the Thanksgiving 10K, a different race, or just rebuild. Each one shapes a different four to six weeks, and I would rather plan toward something real than guess.
